hero.title: Ashtangika Marga: The Eightfold Path
hero.description: The 'Middle Way' preached by Gautama Buddha to eliminate suffering (Dukkha) and attain Nirvana.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Components

  • Panna (Wisdom): Right View, Resolve
  • Sila (Conduct): Speech, Action, Livelihood
  • Samadhi (Mental Discipline): Effort, Mindfulness, Concentration

Philosophy

  • Antimarga: The Middle Path between self-indulgence and self-mortification.

Structure of the Path

  • Wisdom (Prajna)
    • Right View: Understanding Four Noble Truths.
    • Right Resolve: Intention of renunciation/goodwill.
  • Ethical Conduct (Sila)
    • Right Speech: No lying, slander, or harsh talk.
    • Right Action: No killing, stealing, or misconduct.
    • Right Livelihood: Not engaging in trade of weapons, poison, or beings.
  • Mental Discipline (Samadhi)
    • Right Effort: Preventing unwholesome states.
    • Right Mindfulness: Awareness of body/mind.
    • Right Concentration: Deep states of meditation (Jhana).
CategoryConstituents
WisdomSamma-ditthi, Samma-sankappa
ConductSamma-vaca, Samma-kammanta, Samma-ajiva
MentalSamma-vayama, Samma-sati, Samma-samadhi

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Evolution of Buddhist thought from the life of Buddha to the institutionalization of the path.

cards.details: Life of Siddhartha Gautama; Enlightenment at Bodh Gaya and the First Sermon at Sarnath (Dharmachakrapravartana) where the 8-fold path was first articulated.
Ashoka the Great patronizes Buddhism, formalizing the practice of the Eightfold Path across the Maurya Empire through Edicts.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics for Prelims
mnemonics.description: Remember the three divisions of the path (Trisiksha).

items.title: S.M.C
items.decryption: Sila (Ethics: Right Speech, Action, Livelihood), Samadhi (Meditation: Effort, Mindfulness, Concentration), Panna (Wisdom: View, Resolve).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Candidates often confuse the Eightfold Path with the Four Noble Truths. The Path is the 4th Noble Truth (Dukkha Nirodha Gamini Pratipada).
Do not assume the path is purely spiritual; it contains socio-economic components like 'Right Livelihood'.
